weakness: The top grasp only varied the grasp point and wrist tilt around the object. With the object lying 7 mm from a 5 cm tall container wall, the hand body (about 20 cm wide along the finger-closing axis, only ~4 cm above the grip point) collided with the wall for every candidate, so the planner refused all descents and the program gave up without touching anything.
how_found: Questioned A1 (free space beside the object along the closing axis). In Phase 1 two seeds already needed a lateral shift and a tilt to fit next to the bowl, which showed the margin was only a few millimetres.
why_missed: I thought of clearance as finger clearance (the opening is 8 cm vs a 4.3 cm object), not hand clearance, and assumed the scene always leaves room for some top-down approach; the official init states happen to keep about 6-9 cm between the two objects.
fix: When every grasp candidate is refused, relocate the blocker: pick the nearest small movable neighbour by its far-side wall, carry it to the free spot (scored with all obstacle boxes, validated by the planner) and set it down, then grasp again. Also: try both lateral shift directions, re-check holding after the lift, and use obstacle boxes (fixture parts included) instead of object centres for neighbour distances. Pushing or dragging the object itself was tried first and was unreliable (fingertip drag slips by friction balance; end pushes along the long axis did not move it far enough from a round wall and ran into a low stove).
general_rule: When no collision-free grasp exists because a movable neighbour is in the way of the hand (not just the fingers), move the neighbour away first (or change the scene) instead of only varying the grasp pose; and estimate clearance with the full hand geometry along the closing axis, not the finger opening.

weakness: The place target (the container) was detected once, right after the lift, and the hand then flew to that stale position and released. When the container slid ~10 cm during the carry, the object was dropped on the table where the container had been.
how_found: Questioned A8 (the place target does not move after detection). The detection happens 4-5 s before the release, which is a long open-loop window for anything a person or another robot might touch.
why_missed: I treated perception as a one-shot step before motion, and the noise-averaging I added made the single snapshot feel trustworthy; nothing in the base scene ever moves.
fix: place_in_container(): re-detect the container (averaged) after moving above it and again after the descent; if it moved more than 2 cm, re-target and repeat (lifting first if already low), up to 6 times, before opening the gripper.
general_rule: Re-perceive the goal location immediately before every irreversible step (release, insertion, contact) and re-target if it moved, instead of acting on a detection taken before a long motion.

weakness: Every grasp candidate used a vertical (straight-down) gripper. With the object at the far edge of the workspace (0.83 m from the base) there is no IK solution for a vertical wrist at table height, so every candidate was refused; the program then misdiagnosed this as 'blocked by a neighbour', relocated an unrelated object, and its relative lift-after-failure accumulated until targets left the workspace bounds. Once the object was held, a carry that stopped half-way dropped it and the program released the gripper over nothing without noticing.
how_found: Questioned the implicit reach assumption behind A1/A5: the candidate list only varied position and a sideways tilt, so I suspected that any place the vertical wrist cannot reach would be fatal. Screening other axes first (heavier/slippery object, other object shapes, scaled bowl/object, object on its side) showed the program already tolerated those.
why_missed: The default init states put everything in the comfortable middle of the workspace, and the earlier fixes were all about collisions, so I equated 'refused' with 'collision' and never considered kinematic reach.
fix: Added grasp candidates whose approach leans forward, away from the robot base, by 0.25/0.45/0.65 rad about the finger-closing axis (with a slightly higher grip-height range); failure retreats go to an absolute safe height instead of a relative lift; the carry retries through a high mid-waypoint if a move is refused/stopped; holding is re-checked before descent and release, and a lost object is picked up again (up to 3 pick-place cycles).
general_rule: When every motion to a target is refused, distinguish unreachable (kinematics) from blocked (collision) and answer reach failures with a different approach direction leaning away from the base, not with scene changes; and make retry motions absolute so repeated attempts cannot drift out of the workspace.

weakness: The program assumed the container is empty: it released the object over the container centre, where it came to rest on a block already inside the bowl (block top level with the rim) without touching the bowl, so the 'on/in' contact check failed every time.
how_found: Questioned A16 (nothing is already in or on the place target). Real containers are often partly filled, and the release step never looked at what is inside.
why_missed: Place targets were treated as a point (the container centre) rather than as free space inside the container; the base scene's bowl is always empty.
fix: Six repair iterations, best 0.4 (base and earlier variations stayed >= 0.9): (1) detect occupants inside the container footprint and try to take them out first - impossible with this API, because open_gripper() always opens to 8 cm and the open fingers hit the bowl rim around a 5 cm block (no partial-width opening); (2-3) release off-centre on the free side - the object still rested flat on the block top, which is above the rim; (4-5) tilt the hand 0.5/0.9 rad about the closing axis so the free end dips into the gap between block and wall - works in some seeds; (6) choose the free side away from the robot and fall back to the other side when the release pose is refused - still 0.3-0.4. Marked unsolved and the pipeline reverted to the round-3 version.
general_rule: Before releasing into a container, perceive what is already inside and plan the release into the actual free volume (or clear it first); check that your gripper can physically fit the clearing grasp (opening width vs. container wall) before relying on it.

weakness: The grasp was aimed at a single (noise-averaged) snapshot of the object. While the object slid steadily at 1.2 cm/s, the fingers closed where it had been, and grasps that did catch it were pulled out of the hand by the ongoing motion; the 5 retries ran out before the motion ended in most seeds.
how_found: Questioned A7 (the object is static between detection and closing). Round 2 had shown the target can move; the object being grasped can move just as well (tray, conveyor, a person nudging it), and the retry loop only succeeded by luck once the motion stopped.
why_missed: Averaging 8 detections made a moving object look like a precise static one: averaging removes noise but hides motion, and I never looked at detections over time.
fix: Before every grasp attempt, track the object for 2 s (arm still), fit its planar velocity by least squares (resolves ~3 mm/s despite 1 cm noise) and wait in 2 s steps (up to 60 s) until it is below 6 mm/s, then grasp.
general_rule: Before acting on an object, estimate its velocity from a short time series of detections (not from a single or averaged snapshot) and wait for it to settle or predict its motion; averaging repeated detections removes noise but silently hides motion.

weakness: The object was carried and released in the hand yaw used for the grasp. With a tall post 1.2 cm beside the container, in line with the hand's wide finger-closing axis, the move above the container and the descent were refused; the program ignored the refusal and opened the gripper wherever the hand had stopped (a waypoint beside the bowl), dropping the object on the table.
how_found: Questioned A9 (free space around the place target for the hand). Round 1 had shown that the hand is ~20 cm wide along the closing axis, but that lesson was only applied to the grasp, not to the release.
why_missed: I treated the place step as 'move the grip point above the target', with orientation copied from the grasp, and I did not check the result of the descent before the irreversible release.
fix: place_in_container() now tries hand yaws (0, 90, +45, -45 deg about the vertical, the object is symmetric under these for a drop) when the move above the container or the descent is refused, and never releases after a refused descent; as a last resort it returns over the container before releasing.
general_rule: Before any irreversible action, check that the preceding approach motion actually succeeded; when an approach is refused, search the free degrees of freedom of the end-effector (e.g. yaw about the approach axis) instead of acting from wherever the arm stopped.
